# Appeal of Denial — Knee Arthroscopy / Meniscus Surgery (CPT 29881)

**RE:** Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination, Reference No. POC-E2AA78E9EC-43782
**Member:** Harper Delgado
**Member ID:** W267205200
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-09
**Governing policy:** Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Prior Authorization Tip Sheet (Evolent_CG-316) — https://www1.radmd.com/sites/default/files/2024-02/2023%20Knee%20Arthroscopy%20Clin%20Tip%20Sheet%20Evolent%2002282024.pdf

Dear Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Appeals Department,

I am writing to formally request reconsideration of the denial of my prior authorization request for knee arthroscopy/meniscus surgery (CPT 29881). My denial notice states that the documentation submitted was "incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." My surgeon, Dr. Reyes, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in my file address the categories of information the plan's own guideline says should be reviewed.

**What the plan's guideline asks for.** The Evolent Knee Arthroscopy Tip Sheet states:

> "The guidelines should be reviewed for additional requirements including duration of symptoms, physical examination, and radiographic criteria and for the complete listing of other procedures not included below."

I want to note plainly that the specific listed criteria I was given for this appeal are the ones the tip sheet provides for lateral release and for debridement/chondroplasty of patellofemoral chondrosis — not a separately-quoted section for meniscectomy (my actual procedure). I have not been given, and am not quoting, any policy language written specifically for meniscus repair/meniscectomy. However, the general categories the guideline directs reviewers to consider — duration of symptoms, physical examination findings, conservative treatment, and radiographic findings — are all documented in my record, and I am addressing each below.

**Duration of symptoms.** My chart documents 18 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest.

**Conservative (non-operative) treatment.** The guideline's list of non-operative measures includes:

> "oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, analgesics, tramadol o Brace/orthosis o Physical therapy modalities o Supervised home exercise o Weight optimization o Corticosteroid injection"

and

> "o Rest or activity modifications/limitations o Ice/heat o Protected weight bearing o Pharmacologic treatment:"

My record shows that I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (20 visits, 2026-03-26 to 2026-07-02) focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note; took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief; and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-13, which gave only two weeks of partial relief. This treatment history reflects the same categories of non-operative care the guideline lists, sustained over a period longer than the shortest duration referenced in the tip sheet for the procedures it does list in detail.

**Physical examination.** My chart documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain, along with locking, giving way, and inability to squat or kneel, with function limited to level walking.

**Radiographic/imaging findings.** My MRI of 2026-07-14 shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking, and articular cartilage that is preserved, with a Kellgren-Lawrence grade of 1. The guideline states:

> "MRI should not be the primary tool used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

and separately sets out the Kellgren-Lawrence grading scale, in which a grade of 1 reflects only "Possible joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation." My case does not turn on arthritic change — my MRI documents a structural, mechanical tear causing locking, not degenerative joint disease. My low Kellgren-Lawrence grade and preserved cartilage support that this is a discrete meniscal injury rather than an arthritic process, which is consistent with (not contradicted by) the guideline's caution about using MRI to assess arthritis severity.

**Summary.** Between my physical therapy records, medication and injection history, examination findings, and MRI, the record documents symptom duration, physical examination findings, conservative treatment, and radiographic findings — the categories the plan's own guideline identifies as relevant to review. I am not aware of, and have not been shown, any specific published criterion for meniscectomy (CPT 29881) that my record fails to meet. I ask that the plan identify precisely which specific requirement it believes is missing, or reverse the denial based on the documentation already submitted.

**Request.** I ask that Harvard Pilgrim Health Care reconsider this denial and approve coverage for CPT 29881, or, if information is still considered missing, tell me and Dr. Reyes exactly what additional documentation is needed so it can be provided before a final decision.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-05**. Please direct this appeal and any questions to Member Services at **1-888-333-4742**, and to the appeal address printed on my denial letter.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Harper Delgado
Member ID: W267205200
Date: [insert date of signing]
Contact phone: [insert phone number]
Contact address: [insert mailing address]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
